name: open-cursor
description: Use any supported AI provider in Cursor through one guided setup

openCursorModels.proxyPort.description: Port for the local OpenAI-compatible routing proxy.

openCursorModels.modelPrefix.description: Prefix added to custom model names in Cursor to avoid conflicts with built-in models.

openCursorModels.autoStartProxy.description: After initial setup, start the proxy automatically when Cursor launches.

openCursorModels.logRequests.description: Log proxied request paths and routes to the Open Cursor Models output channel.

openCursorModels.logRequestBodies.description: Log each proxied request's detected agent role, tool names, turn count, and a system-prompt preview. Useful for verifying subagent detection; may include prompt text in the output channel.

openCursorModels.forceSubagentModel.description: Route requests detected as subagent (Task tool) runs to a fixed model, ignoring the model the orchestrating agent selected. Detection is heuristic — verify with logRequestBodies first.

openCursorModels.subagentModel.description: Model used for subagent runs when forceSubagentModel is enabled. Accepts a profile display name, slug, or the full prefixed Cursor model name.

openCursorModels.tunnelProvider.description: Tunnel provider. Auto tries ngrok, then cloudflared.

enumDescriptions: Use Cursor's OpenAI API Key field and oc- model names.
Use Cursor's Anthropic API Key field and claude-oc- model names.
Recommended. Use Cursor's Google API Key field and gemini-oc- model names.
openCursorModels.providerSlot.description: Which Cursor API key field carries the generated OpenCursor proxy key.

scripts.test: npm run typecheck && node --import tsx --test test/**/*.test.ts
